name: Desktop Dock app
summary: Carnivore runs as a regular Mac app in the Dock: closing the window leaves it running, the Dock icon shows how many sessions wait on you, a Dock menu starts new work, and a full menu bar (File, Edit, View, Session, Window, Help) acts on the session in view.
where: The Dock icon and its right-click menu while the desktop app runs.
The Mac menu bar at the top of the screen: Carnivore, File, Edit, View, Session, Window, Help.
how_to: Click the Dock icon to bring the window back where you left it; closing the window does not quit the app or stop the engine.
Read the red number on the Dock icon: it is how many sessions are waiting on you, the same count as the menu bar icon's Need You row.
Right-click or hold the Dock icon for New Session, Recent Projects and the sessions waiting on you.
Watch the Dock icon hop once when a new question arrives while Carnivore is behind other windows.
Use File, Session and Window in the menu bar: New Session, New Window, Restart, Stop, Rename, Answer Waiting Question, which act on the session you are looking at.
Turn the menu bar icon off or on in settings, desktop app, show menu bar icon; the Dock app is unaffected.
examples: Close the window, keep working in the terminal app, and see the Dock badge turn 2 when two agents ask for you.
Right-click the Dock icon and pick a recent project to start a session in it.
Press Cmd-Q for a one-time notice that the engine keeps your agents running.
media_exempt: native: the macOS Dock, its badge and menu, and the system menu bar, which no browser capture can show
